metadata.title: SpatialMeet - A Virtual Office You Can Walk Around
metadata.description: SpatialMeet is a free virtual office in your browser. Walk around a pixel-art floor with your team and start a video call just by standing next to someone.

items.a: SpatialMeet is a virtual office you walk around in. Your team appears as pixel-art characters on a shared 2D floor, and a video or voice call starts when you stand next to someone instead of when you click a meeting link.

items.q: Do I need to install anything?
items.a: No. SpatialMeet runs in the browser on desktop and mobile. Open a room link and you are inside the office.
Yes. Creating rooms, walking around, chatting and calling are free.

items.q: Do I need an account to join a room?
items.a: No. Anyone can join as a guest with just a name. Signing in only adds a saved profile, a character you keep, and a list of your rooms.

items.q: How do the video calls work?
items.a: Calls run peer-to-peer over WebRTC, so audio and video travel straight between browsers. Once a call is connected it stays connected until someone hangs up or leaves the room. Walking away will not drop it.

items.q: Is my camera on the whole time I am in a room?
items.a: No. The camera and microphone are opened only for a call and released the moment it ends.

items.q: Can I use SpatialMeet on a phone?
items.a: Yes. On touch devices you move with an on-screen joystick, and the call controls adapt to the smaller screen.

items.q: How is this different from a normal video call?
items.a: A normal call puts everyone in one grid until the meeting ends. A SpatialMeet room stays open all day, so you can see who is around, drift between conversations, and talk to the people you walk over to.

gather.label: Gather alternative

meta.title: Free Gather Alternative in Your Browser
meta.description: Looking for a free Gather alternative? SpatialMeet is a pixel-art virtual office with proximity video calls. No trial, no per-seat price, nothing to install.

gather.title: A free Gather alternative.
gather.subtitle: Gather dropped its free plan and now charges per member. SpatialMeet keeps the same idea, an office you walk around and talk in, and keeps it free.

points.title: No trial clock
points.body: Gather gives you 30 days before you pay. SpatialMeet has no trial, because there is nothing to upgrade to.

points.title: Nothing to install
points.body: Everything runs in the browser on desktop and mobile. Share a link and your team is inside in seconds.

points.title: Guests walk straight in
points.body: Anyone with the link joins with just a name. Accounts are optional and only keep your profile and rooms.

faq.a: No. Gather no longer has a permanent free plan. It offers a 30-day trial, then the Essential plan starts at $12 per member per month. SpatialMeet is free.

faq.q: What does Gather have that SpatialMeet does not?
faq.a: Gather has screen sharing, AI meeting notes and office customization. SpatialMeet focuses on the core: walking around, proximity calls, a meeting table, chat, a whiteboard and room music.

faq.q: Can I move my team from Gather to SpatialMeet?
faq.a: Yes. Create a room, share its link, and everyone walks in. There is no data to migrate and nothing to install.

faq.q: How many people fit in a SpatialMeet room?
faq.a: A room holds up to 20 people at once, and you can open as many rooms as you need.

them.price: Business from $16 per user per month

faq.a: Kumospace has a free plan for up to 5 registered members, with one floor and guests limited to 4 hours a week. The Business plan starts at $16 per user per month. SpatialMeet is free for everyone.

faq.q: What does Kumospace have that SpatialMeet does not?
faq.a: Kumospace includes screen sharing, and its paid plans add recording and unlimited chat history. SpatialMeet does not have screen sharing or recording yet.

faq.q: Do my teammates need an account?
faq.a: No. Anyone with a room link can join as a guest with just a name. Signing in only keeps a saved profile, a character and a list of your rooms.
Yes. It runs in mobile browsers with an on-screen joystick, so there is no app to download.

points.title: An office, not an event
points.body: Rooms do not end when a meeting does. The same link works tomorrow, and people drop in when they are free.

points.title: Walk over to talk
points.body: Get close to a teammate to start a video or voice call. Sit at the meeting table and everyone there joins one call.

them.price: Day Pass $5 per user per day, Business from $399 per month
them.freePlan: 2 hours a day, up to 12 people

faq.a: SpatialChat has a free plan with up to 2 hours of meetings a day for up to 12 participants. Paid options include a $5 Day Pass per user and Business plans from $399 per month. SpatialMeet is free with no daily limit.

faq.q: Is SpatialMeet good for virtual events?
faq.a: SpatialMeet is made for groups that meet every day. Rooms hold 20 people at a time, so it suits team offices, study groups and small meetups more than large events.

faq.q: What does SpatialChat have that SpatialMeet does not?
faq.a: SpatialChat supports screen sharing, pinned files and large events. SpatialMeet does not have screen sharing yet, and focuses on everyday presence and quick conversations.
Yes. SpatialMeet calls run peer to peer over WebRTC, so audio and video go straight between browsers.

workadventure.title: A WorkAdventure alternative with room to grow.

points.title: Twice the room

points.title: No map to build
points.body: Every room comes with an office floor, a meeting table, a whiteboard and a speaker. Create a room and walk in.

points.title: Nothing to host

them.price: Business from €8 per user per month

faq.a: WorkAdventure has a free plan for up to 10 simultaneous users. The Business plan starts at €8 per user per month, and event pricing starts at €4 per user per day. SpatialMeet is free.

faq.q: Can I customize the map in SpatialMeet?
faq.a: Not yet. Every room uses the same office floor. WorkAdventure lets you design your own maps, which suits teams that want a custom world.

faq.q: Do I need to run a server?
faq.a: No. SpatialMeet is hosted for you. Create a room in the browser and share the link.

faq.q: How do calls start in SpatialMeet?
faq.a: Walk up to a teammate and their call bar appears. One tap starts video or voice. At the meeting table, everyone who sits down joins the same call.

A room holds up to 20 people at once, and you can open as many rooms as you need.

proximityChat.label: Proximity chat

meta.title: Free Proximity Video Chat in the Browser
meta.description: Proximity chat for teams and friends: walk your character up to someone to start a video or voice call. Free, in the browser, no download.

proximityChat.title: Proximity chat that starts when you walk over.
proximityChat.subtitle: In SpatialMeet, where you stand decides who you talk to. Walk up to someone to call them, sit at the table to talk as a group, and walk on when you are done.

points.title: Getting close starts it
points.body: Stand next to a teammate and a call bar appears. One tap opens video or voice.

points.title: Groups at the table
points.body: Sit at the meeting table and you join the call with everyone sitting there.

points.title: Peer to peer
points.body: Calls travel straight between browsers over WebRTC, so there is nothing to install.

faq.a: Proximity chat connects you with people based on where your character is. You talk to the people near you, the way you would in a real room.

faq.q: Does the call end when I walk away?
faq.a: No. Once a call is connected it stays connected until someone hangs up, so walking around does not drop it.

faq.q: Can more than two people talk?
faq.a: Yes. Call someone who is already on a call to join them, or sit at the meeting table to talk as a group.
Yes. SpatialMeet is free in the browser on desktop and mobile.
